title: Complete groups forced zero predecessor-minus-successor scores in 64 of 68 deep ComCat groups in 2000-2025
abstract: We tested time direction in close deep-earthquake groups. We used 785 ComCat events with preferred magnitude at least 5.5 and depth greater than 300 km in 2000-2025. At 200 km chord distance and seven days, 101 events had a predecessor and 102 had a successor. The difference was -1. Annual regional time shuffles gave a mean of 0.003 and a central 95% range of -3 to 3 in 9,999 draws. The upper-tail p value was 0.8219. An added graph check found 64 complete groups among 68 connected groups. A complete group with distinct times must have equal predecessor and successor counts. Only one observed group gave a nonzero difference. Thus this score discards much of the observed sequence structure. Its null result does not show that triggering is absent. Other windows and spatial controls also gave no clear positive excess. The study adds a method limit to prior pair-count and magnitude-order results on the same records. Exchangeability, catalog error, sparse data and fixed windows limit inference. Code, aggregate scores, a proof, source hashes and an independent numerical audit are included. Event records remain external.

display.caption: Observed direction scores and conditional shuffle ranges. Ranges describe the null model, not uncertainty in a physical effect. Complete groups force this score to zero.
